title: The cooking competition
summary: Two brothers enter a TV cooking show and learn that working as a team is harder than cooking.
paragraphs: Rafa and Diego had always cooked together. As children they made terrible pancakes on Sunday mornings; as adults they cooked for every family celebration. So when a TV programme announced a competition for {{amateur}} cooking teams, their sister filled in the form for them as a joke. Three weeks later they were standing in a studio, under bright lights, in front of four cameras.

The first challenge was simple: make a dish with eggs, potatoes and one surprise ingredient. The surprise was {{octopus}}. Rafa wanted to make a Spanish omelette with grilled octopus on top. Diego wanted to make a warm potato salad. They argued for five of their thirty minutes. In the end they did both, badly. The judges said the dish had "no clear idea".

That night, in the hotel, the brothers hardly spoke. Then Diego said, "At home, you always do the main dish and I always do the sauces. Why are we both trying to do everything here?" Rafa thought about it. He realised that the cameras had made them both nervous and {{competitive}}, even with each other.

The next day they changed their {{strategy}}. Before each challenge they spent two minutes deciding on one idea and who would do what. They stopped arguing and started tasting each other's work. Their dishes became simpler and better. In the semi-final they made a fish stew with a bright green herb oil, and one of the judges asked for a second spoon.

They didn't win. They finished third, after a mother and daughter from Galicia and two retired firefighters. But they went home happier than when they arrived. Six months later they opened a small food stall at the weekend market. The sign above it says "Two brothers, one idea", and the menu is short: one main dish, one {{sauce}}, one dessert, every week something new.

amateur.meaning: doing something for pleasure, not as a job

octopus.meaning: a sea animal with eight long arms

competitive.meaning: wanting very much to win or be better than others

sauce.meaning: a thick liquid served with food to give it more flavour

options: At home they each had their own job, but in the studio they both tried to do everything.
